messages.author: f1572a038d61492c
messages.subject: inla.fmesher.write.file() error on cluster
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to fit a basic logistic regression model with one random effect, but the number of rows in my data frame is about 9 million. I'm running this on a cluster and keep getting the following error:

Error in file(filename, "wb") : cannot open the connection
Calls: inla -> inla.write.fmesher.file -> file
In addition: There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)

The IT person in my department and I think this is likely related to INLA writing temporary files that are too large for the /tmp directory on the cluster (which has much smaller memory than the node itself). 

Is there a way to change the directory to which INLA writes tmp files? Or perhaps a way to control how much memory these files take up.

Thanks,

Jessica Godwin

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.fmesher.write.file() error on cluster
parts:
Hi,
Partly depending on your model structure, you may not be able to run your model anyway, but I think all of the tmp file writing uses the R interface to obtain the names of temporary files. You would therefore have to tell R itself to use a tmp directory on a different drive with more allowed capacity.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.fmesher.write.file() error on cluster
parts:
Hi,
I had forgotten about that option! Daniel Simpson mentioned it in this thread:
https://groups.google.com/forum/m/#!topic/r-inla-discussion-group/hIll4XwS0_Y
and it appears it should set the temp directory for the inla() call, so try that first. But if you get the error also for fmesher related tmp files, then you’d have to tell R instead. (But if you were writing that large triangulation meshes you’d be in even bigger trouble with your model...)

Finn

There's nothing spatial about my model (YET!)... just a very large discrete hazards model with survey data from multiple countries.

I tried to run it with the working.directory specified to a larger, writable directory. The call ran for (much, much!) longer, but is breaking with an error after about an hour with an error that it cannot read the model.ini file:

> full.mod.inla <- inla(formula.full.inla, family = 'binomial',
+                       control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE),
+                       data = all.births, verbose = T, num.threads = 2,
+       working.directory = '~/INLAworking')
Model and results are stored in working directory [~/INLAworking-1]


*** ERROR *** Fail to parse ini-file[~/INLAworking-1/Model.ini]....


hgid: 29c6a7f1b1ff  date: Thu Jun 15 19:50:23 2017 +0800
Report bugs to <he...@r-inla.org>
Processing file [~/INLAworking-1/Model.ini] max_threads=[2]
inla_build...

It's unclear to me how early on the inla() call is breaking. This appears to still be a file opening issue.
